mstts:express-as.prosody: As we wrap up, let's remember that the story of Katyn isn't just about a single tragedy or one chapter of war. It's about how truth and memory can be shaped, challenged, or even hidden by those in power. It's about the quiet bravery of everyday people—families, teachers, artists, and activists—who stand up and say, "No, we won't let these lives be forgotten," even when the world turns away. So, what do you do with a legacy like this? Here are a few things to hold on to: Even the smallest act of remembrance can push back against denial. Art and storytelling have the power to keep memories alive, especially when official accounts try to erase them. Reconciliation isn’t a one-time thing—it’s a long process that takes honesty and patience. Every generation faces a choice: will we inherit silence, or will we go looking for the truth? And maybe most importantly, the fight for justice and dignity is never really done—but every step you take, every time you begin, it matters. The world is full of stories like Katyn. Stories of loss, of denial, and of people striving for recognition. It’s easy to feel small, to think the past is just too far away, or that the forces working to erase it are too strong. But history gets made, and remade, by ordinary people—by all of us. Every time you ask a tough question, light a candle, share a story, or refuse to accept an easy lie, you help carry forward the unfinished work of justice. And remember, you’re never alone on this path. Others have walked it before, and more will follow. The dead aren’t truly lost as long as someone remembers their names. By honoring their memory, you help build a world where truth matters, and where—even the hardest parts of the past—can guide us toward a future that’s more honest and compassionate.
